system_description.narrative_title: Energy shocks, market stress, and regional wars reshaping a fragile global order
system_description.narrative_summary: A convergence of an escalating Middle East war, stressed global energy and shipping chokepoints, and volatile monetary policy is driving acute economic and strategic ripples across markets, states and corporations. Central bank uncertainty and surging yields are amplifying market volatility while China's slowdown and restrained stimulus reshape demand and supply-chain dynamics. Concurrent climate extremes, migration pressures and proxy conflicts in Europe and the Black Sea add humanitarian and operational strain, making the system highly interconnected and sensitive to shocks.
system_description.scope: nation-states and regional security complexes, global energy and commodity markets, international shipping chokepoints, central banks and capital markets, multinational corporations and supply chains, climate-induced disasters and migration flows, and cyber/AI risk vectors
system_description.super_system: the integrated global political-economic system (international order of states, markets, institutions and transnational flows)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets & maritime logistics (oil, LNG, Red Sea/Hormuz/Bab al-Mandeb routes)
International financial system & central banking (bond markets, FX intervention, Fed/BOJ/ECB policy)
Regional security complexes (Middle East conflict dynamics; Russia–Ukraine theatre; European internal security)
Global supply chains & industrial demand (China's economy, autos, semiconductors, manufacturing)

variables.name: US–Iran strategic confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran — together with regional partners and proxy groups (Israel, Gulf states, militias) — are locked in an escalating cycle of strikes and reprisals that is broadening the conflict footprint and reshaping regional deterrence dynamics.

variables.name: Maritime chokepoints and sea-lane warfare
variables.description: State-backed proxies and non‑state actors are mounting attacks on tankers, ports and transits in key sea lanes (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Suez/Bab el‑Mandeb), turning commercial maritime routes into contested spaces and forcing new naval protections, rerouting and insurance shocks.

variables.name: US–China technology and AI rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting leadership in AI, chips and advanced tech via controls, industrial policy, security reviews and diplomatic competition, shifting where technological dominance and supply‑chain resilience will be built.

variables.name: Global monetary credibility and market stress
variables.description: Major central banks and financial markets — notably the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan — are facing renewed credibility and policy‑expectation shocks as bond yields surge, currency intervention risks rise and market signalling forces reprice global capital flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine energy and infrastructure warfare
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine are increasingly striking and targeting energy and logistics infrastructure while states impose sanctions and export controls, driving disruptions in European energy supplies and amplifying global commodity and food‑security risks.
